A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effects induced on the normal state magnetization by the superconducting fluctuating pairs are due to the presence of the superconductivity itself and that they are not due to the presence, in the normal state, of the superfluid pairs that are responsible for the superconductivity.
the superconducting correlations in Pb1-xInx alloys, in the normal state, are suppressed by the application of a magnetic field of amplitude above Hc2 (0).

the superconducting fluctuating effects in Pb_{1+x}In_x alloys above Hc2 (0) are due to the shrinking of the Cooper pairs wave function, which is limited by the uncertainty principle, and are not related to the existence of the superconductivity itself.

the superconducting fluctuating pairs are coherent, and they are the ones responsible for all the superconducting effects observed above Hc2.
